adapters.says: Codex's command-line runtime runs one non-interactive turn per invocation: `codex exec <PROMPT>` carries the prompt to completion and exits. What this row names is MEASURED PRESENCE and not measured behaviour -- on 2026-09-18, on this machine, `codex --version` reported `codex-cli 0.154.0`, `codex doctor` reported auth mode `chatgpt` with 22 checks ok and 0 failed, and every flag below was read in `codex exec --help` (ADR-017 amendment 5). No run of this adapter has been observed by the dispatch port, in this repository or anywhere else, so every sentence about what these flags DO remains a claim, and the row is honest rather than green. `-C/--cd <DIR>` runs the turn in a directory named on the command line -- named here as the tree the PORT placed, and never `--worktree`, which would have this product place a tree of its own and give isolation a second home (Cardinal III). `-s/--sandbox workspace-write` is the declared form of ADR-017 decision 5's isolation: this product's own confinement of its writes to the directory it is working in, stated as a claim by its publisher, layered UNDER the kit's own isolation and never instead of it -- the kit's guarantee is the leased tree plus the judgement on return, and a vendor's sandbox flag is a second belt whose behaviour this kit has not measured. `-o/--output-last-message <FILE>` writes the turn's final message to a file, which is how the worker's ARTIFACT comes back as a file with a declared shape rather than as a transcript somebody parsed; the port provides that file, outside the worker's tree, so the answer is not mistaken for a change to the repository. What this adapter deliberately does NOT declare: `--output-schema` (which would need the port to provide a path to a declared shape, and does not yet), `fork`, and `--skip-git-repo-check` (the tree the port places is a linked working tree of a real repository, so the check should pass -- UNVERIFIED, and this is the first thing a real run will either confirm or refute). Nor -- and this is the C4 decision, taken with the round-trip BUILT and available -- `asks` or `resumes`. `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` and `resume --last` were both read in `--help` on 2026-09-18, so a way back in demonstrably exists; what does not exist is a way for this port to learn WHICH session without becoming a reader of this product's output. The session id is carried in the `--json` event stream, and an `asks.reentry` channel pointing at that stream would make the port parse JSONL it has no declared grammar for -- the port reads a declared channel whole and never interprets what is in it. `resume --last` needs no id and is refused for a different reason: it names a session by recency on this machine, not the session of THIS task, so two dispatches in flight would each be resumed into whichever ran last -- a name agreeing on the word and disagreeing on the referent (Cardinal VII). There is also no measured exit code meaning 'I need input'. So this intelligence cannot reach `input-required` through this adapter, which is an honest absence: what it would take is an `-o`-style flag that writes the session id to a file the port provides, or a documented ending, and either one is a row edited here and nothing else. Route options: the model, effort and (where the product has one) spend cap a route cell declares are passed as -m, -c -- flags read from the installed product's own --help on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.301, codex-cli 0.154.0), 2026-10-16. A turn cap has no flag here, so the port's wall-time stop condition is the cap every product honours.
